## The gate-scratch volume is IN SERVICE — verified on the host and in CloudWatch

Independently verified at 2026-09-06 ~02:55 UTC, after the runbook was executed. This is the state
change this ticket exists to produce: gate scratch is no longer on the root filesystem.

### Host state

```
mountpoint -q /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch   ->  MOUNTED

NAME          FSTYPE SIZE MOUNTPOINT
nvme1n1       xfs     50G /var/gerrit
nvme0n1               60G
├─nvme0n1p1   xfs     60G /
└─nvme0n1p128 vfat    10M /boot/efi
nvme2n1       xfs     50G /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch     <- was RAW, no FSTYPE, unmounted

/etc/fstab:
UUID=7ea719fd-f65c-4e8f-992c-d74410b5ea4c /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch xfs defaults,nofail 0 2
```

Mounted **by UUID**, not by device name — which matters on Nitro, where NVMe device naming is not
stable across boots and a `/dev/nvme2n1` fstab entry would be a latent boot failure.

### Both markers present, on their intended (different) filesystems

```
-rw-r--r--. root root 0 Sep  6 02:45  /var/lib/rebar/.gate-scratch-required        <- on ROOT
-rw-r--r--. root root 0 Sep  6 02:45  /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch/.gate-scratch-mounted  <- on the VOLUME
```

That split is the whole point of the design: the declaration survives an unmount while the proof
disappears with the volume, so "declaration present + proof absent" is a state gate admission can
detect and refuse on, rather than silently repopulating the store on root.

### Space reclaimed — the disk-pressure win

```
df /                 60G   34G   27G   57%      <- was 42G used / 70%, and 49G / 81% at its worst
df gate-scratch      50G  2.7G   48G    6%
```

Root fell **70% -> 57%**, roughly 8 GB returned, with 2.7 GB of gate scratch now living on its own
50 GB volume at 6% utilisation. The root filesystem is no longer the thing a review burst fills.

### The consumer actually sees it

Verified from *inside* the review-bot container, not merely on the host:

```
docker exec compose-review-bot-1 df -h /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch
/dev/nvme2n1     50G  2.7G   48G   6% /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch
```

This is the check that distinguishes a real fix from a host-only mount the containers never see.

### CloudWatch agrees, and the alarms cleared to OK rather than going blind

```
gate_scratch_mounted            latest datapoint = 1.0   (was 0.0 on every sample)
rebar-gate-scratch-unmounted    OK   (state updated 19:46:55)
rebar-gate-scratch-disk-high    OK   (state updated 19:46:44)
```

I checked the state values explicitly rather than inferring from the alarms merely leaving the ALARM
list. **OK is not the same as INSUFFICIENT_DATA**, and given this host's live probe-truncation defect
(metrics near the tail of the probe publish nothing, so alarms can leave ALARM by going blind rather
than by recovering) that distinction had to be established, not assumed. Both are genuinely OK on
real datapoints.

### Not yet ticked

The `[non-codebase]` acceptance criteria require an indented `provenance:` continuation line naming
environment, principal, privilege posture and instrument before they can be marked complete — the
close gate enforces this, and rightly so. I am recording the evidence here first; the AC ticks plus
their provenance lines follow, and that edit will stale the plan-review attestation and require a
fresh review before the close.
